rows.label: Concept
rows.text: A pure semiconductor has equal electrons and holes. Doping makes n-type material, with electron majority carriers, or p-type material, with hole majority carriers. A junction conducts when the p-side is positive. In a transistor, β = I_c / I_b, so a small base current controls a larger collector current.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Silicon's forward drop is about 0.7 V. Germanium's is about 0.3 V.  ·  The depletion layer has very few mobile charges.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: An intrinsic semiconductor is a pure crystal. At room temperature a few bonds break, giving equal numbers of free electrons and holes. Heating frees more pairs, so the conductivity rises.  ·  An extrinsic semiconductor has been doped. A group-15 atom adds a spare electron and makes n-type material, in which electrons are the majority carriers. A group-13 atom leaves a hole and makes p-type material.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Intrinsic semiconductor  ·  Doping  ·  Forward bias  ·  Current gain

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Intrinsic means pure.  ·  n-type electrons, p-type holes.  ·  Forward bias conducts.  ·  A small base current controls a larger collector current.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Force on moving charge F = q(v×B); on a wire F = BIL sinθ.  ·  Faraday: EMF ε = −dΦ/dt; Lenz's law gives the sign (induced current opposes the change in flux).

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: The doped crystal is still electrically neutral. The extra carriers come with the atom's nuclear charge. n-type does not mean the lump of silicon is negative.  ·  A p-n junction has a depletion layer. Forward bias, with the p-side positive, lowers the barrier and current flows. Silicon needs about 0.7 V before that current becomes large. Reverse bias widens the barrier and only a leakage current flows.  ·  A bipolar transistor has emitter, base and collector. A small base current controls a much larger collector current. The current gain β is I_c / I_b.
